title: Canonical graded comparison from ideal-power quotient isomorphisms
statement:
Let $\varphi:A\to C$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $I\subseteq A$, $J\subseteq C$ be ideals with $\varphi(I)\subseteq J$. Use the quotient and ideal-power conventions of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] and the associated graded rings of [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. For $n\ge1$, let $Q_n(\varphi):A/I^n\to C/J^n$ be $[a]\mapsto[\varphi(a)]$. The homogeneous formulas
$$G_r(\varphi):I^r/I^{r+1}\longrightarrow J^r/J^{r+1},\qquad [a]_r\longmapsto[\varphi(a)]_r\quad(r\ge0)$$
define a degree-preserving unital graded ring homomorphism $G(\varphi)=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}G_r(\varphi)$. It satisfies $G(\varphi)((a\bmod I)x)=(\varphi(a)\bmod J)G(\varphi)(x)$ for every $a\in A$ and $x\in\operatorname{gr}_I(A)$. If every $Q_n(\varphi)$, $n\ge1$, is an isomorphism, then every $G_r(\varphi)$ and $G(\varphi)$ are isomorphisms; identifying $A/I$ with $C/J$ by $Q_1(\varphi)$ makes $G(\varphi)$ an isomorphism of graded $A/I$-algebras.
For any second ideal-preserving homomorphism $\varphi':(A',I')\to(C',J')$ and homomorphisms $\alpha:A\to A'$, $\gamma:C\to C'$ with $\alpha(I)\subseteq I'$, $\gamma(J)\subseteq J'$ and $\gamma\varphi=\varphi'\alpha$, the canonical maps satisfy
$$Q_n(\gamma)Q_n(\varphi)=Q_n(\varphi')Q_n(\alpha),\qquad G(\gamma)G(\varphi)=G(\varphi')G(\alpha).$$
Here $Q_n$ and $G$ for each of these maps are given by the same representative formulas for its specified source and target ideals. For arbitrary composable ideal-preserving homomorphisms $u:(R,K)\to(S,L)$ and $v:(S,L)\to(T,M)$ of commutative rings, these maps also satisfy $Q_n(vu)=Q_n(v)Q_n(u)$, $G(vu)=G(v)G(u)$, $Q_n(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$ and $G(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$. The functoriality assertions require no quotient isomorphism hypotheses; the isomorphism criterion requires no formal etaleness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), associated-graded conclusion, extracted as a comparison criterion assuming the ideal-power quotient isomorphisms; canonical maps and their functoriality on representatives.

proof.text: For $r\ge1$, $I^r$ consists of finite sums of products of $r$ elements of $I$: induct on $r$ using $I^{r+1}=I^rI$ and absorb any ring coefficient into the last factor. The same holds for $J$. Applying $\varphi$ term by term therefore gives $\varphi(I^r)\subseteq J^r$; for $r=0$ this just says $\varphi(A)\subseteq C$. Consequently $[a]\mapsto[\varphi(a)]$ descends to $Q_n$ for every $n\ge1$, since a difference in $I^n$ maps into $J^n$. The induced map preserves addition, multiplication and $1$ because $\varphi$ does.

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), associated-graded conclusion; elementary representative argument extracting the implication from power-quotient isomorphisms.

proof.text: For $a\in I^r$, define $G_r([a]_r)=[\varphi(a)]_r$. Step 1 puts this in $J^r/J^{r+1}$. If $[a]_r=[b]_r$, the quotient-module coset definition gives $a-b\in I^{r+1}$, so $\varphi(a)-\varphi(b)\in J^{r+1}$ and the target classes agree. The identities $\varphi(a+b)=\varphi(a)+\varphi(b)$ and $\varphi(0)=0$ prove additivity. On the direct sums define $(Gx)_r=G_r(x_r)$; its support is contained in the finite support of $x$, so this is an additive, degree-preserving map.

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), associated-graded conclusion; elementary representative argument extracting the implication from power-quotient isomorphisms.

proof.text: Apply the existing ring-structure theorem to $(A,I)$ and $(C,J)$. For homogeneous representatives its multiplication formula and the ring-map identity give $G_{r+s}([ab]_{r+s})=[\varphi(ab)]_{r+s}=[\varphi(a)\varphi(b)]_{r+s}=G_r([a]_r)G_s([b]_s)$. Every homogeneous class has a representative, so this proves preservation of homogeneous products. Expand two arbitrary elements as finite sums of homogeneous components; distributivity and additivity extend the equality to their products. The degree-zero unit $[1]_0$ maps to $[\varphi(1)]_0=[1]_0$. The same theorem gives the scalar formula: on a homogeneous $[b]_r$, both sides of $G((a\bmod I)[b]_r)=(\varphi(a)\bmod J)G([b]_r)$ equal $[\varphi(a)\varphi(b)]_r$. Additivity extends it to every finite sum.

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), associated-graded conclusion; elementary representative argument extracting the implication from power-quotient isomorphisms.

proof.text: Assume now that every $Q_n$ is an isomorphism. For any $r\ge0$, if $G_r([a]_r)=G_r([b]_r)$, then $\varphi(a-b)\in J^{r+1}$. Thus $Q_{r+1}(\overline{a-b})=0$. Its injectivity implies $a-b\in I^{r+1}$, hence $[a]_r=[b]_r$. This proves injectivity of every $G_r$, using only a positive quotient index even when $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), associated-graded conclusion; elementary representative argument extracting the implication from power-quotient isomorphisms.

proof.text: For $r=0$, $G_0=Q_1$ under $I^0=A$ and $J^0=C$, so it is surjective. For $r\ge1$ and $c\in J^r$, surjectivity of $Q_{r+1}$ supplies $a\in A$ with $\varphi(a)-c\in J^{r+1}$. Ideal powers are descending: every generator $xy$ of $J^rJ$ lies in $J^r$, hence $J^{r+1}\subseteq J^r$. Thus $\varphi(a)\in J^r$ and $Q_r([a])=0$. Injectivity of $Q_r$ gives $a\in I^r$. The element $[a]_r$ is now a legitimate preimage of $[c]_r$ under $G_r$. Together with step 4, this proves homogeneous-piece bijectivity.

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), associated-graded conclusion; elementary representative argument extracting the implication from power-quotient isomorphisms.

proof.text: If $Gx=Gy$, equality of every component and injectivity of $G_r$ give $x_r=y_r$ for every $r$, hence $x=y$. For a target family $y$ supported on a finite set $T$, take the unique preimage $x_r$ of $y_r$ for $r\in T$ and set $x_r=0$ elsewhere. This finite-support family satisfies $Gx=y$. Thus $G$ is bijective. Its inverse respects addition, products and the unit because applying the injective map $G$ to each required identity gives that identity in the target; it preserves degree by the componentwise construction. Transport the $C/J$-algebra structure to an $A/I$-algebra structure via the ring isomorphism $Q_1$. The scalar equality of step 3 then proves that $G$ is an isomorphism of graded $A/I$-algebras.

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), associated-graded conclusion; elementary representative argument extracting the implication from power-quotient isomorphisms.

proof.text: For the commuting square, both $Q_n(\gamma)Q_n(\varphi)$ and $Q_n(\varphi\prime)Q_n(\alpha)$ send $[a]$ to $[\gamma\varphi(a)]=[\varphi\prime\alpha(a)]$. Both graded composites send a homogeneous $[a]_r$ to the same classes in degree $r$ by exactly this equality. Quotient classes have representatives and direct-sum elements are finite sums of homogeneous classes, so these are equal maps. For composable $u,v$, both $Q_n(vu)$ and $Q_n(v)Q_n(u)$ send $[a]$ to $[v(u(a))]$; both $G(vu)$ and $G(v)G(u)$ send $[a]_r$ to $[v(u(a))]_r$. For an identity map these formulas give $[a]\mapsto[a]$ and $[a]_r\mapsto[a]_r$. The same representative and finite-sum arguments give all composition and identity equalities. Steps 1--3 and this step used only ideal preservation, so none of these functoriality assertions assumes quotient isomorphisms or formal etaleness.
